subject: Follow-up: Pricing & regional residency (FinTechCo)
messages:

Subject: FinTechCo intro / pricing framework follow-up

Hi James / Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the immediate follow-ups we discussed:

- Key goals we heard: (1) Productionize customer support summarization and routing, (2) Near-real-time fraud signal enrichment, (3) Embeddings for search across EU and US regions.
- Desired timeline: pilot in 4–6 weeks, full rollout H1 2027.
- Residency requirement: compliance team flagged that customer PII must be processed and stored in EU for EU customers.

A few ask items so we can draft a pricing + deployment proposal:

1) Estimated monthly token volume (generation + contexts) for pilot and steady state. If you can give a low/expected/high split that helps.
2) Budget range for the pilot and for committed annual spend (if available).
3) Target unit economics — is there a target $/1M tokens you’re aiming for?
4) Residency constraints: confirm which datasets must remain in EU vs can be processed in US; any cross-border allowances?

We attached our pricing sheet (redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf) — note the two axes: (A) hosted list pricing (US) and (B) committed/reserved pricing (Dedicated/Private) with discounts. For region: EU-hosted endpoints typically carry a premium (~15–20%) due to regional infra and compliance requirements; Dedicated/Private deployments have different cost profiles and can reduce unit price with a sufficient commit.

Next steps: if you can send volumes + budget by Wednesday, we’ll model three scenarios (hosted US, hosted EU, and Dedicated reserved commit) and propose a target $/1M tokens that maps to your budget. I’ll also loop in Sean to outline a committed discount path if the numbers make sense.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap — helpful. Answers below:

- Volumes (generation + context tokens): pilot (month 1): 30M tokens; expected steady state: ~120M tokens/month; high/peak: up to 300–350M/month during seasonal spikes.
- Embeddings: ~2–3M vectors/month during steady state.
- Budget: pilot budget is constrained (~$2k–$4k/month). For production we have an annual budget conversation target roughly $24k–$72k/year (wide band while leadership aligns).
- Target unit economics: the engineering/finance team said they’d like to get to roughly $6–$10 per 1M tokens on average — anything much above that makes the ROI hard to justify.
- Residency: EU residency is required for EU customer data (both processing and storage). US processing is acceptable for non-EU customer data. Cross-border processing is a no-go for EU PII.

Can you quantify the EU premium and what committed discounts might look like for a 12-month reserved commit? Also please confirm whether embeddings are priced differently in EU vs US.

Best —
James
Head of Product | FinTechCo

Thanks James — that’s exactly the detail we need. I’ll get you three modeled scenarios:

A) Hosted (US endpoints) — best latency/cost; list pricing baseline.
B) Hosted EU endpoints — list pricing + regional premium (we’ll itemize infra premium and additional compliance ops).
C) Dedicated (12-month reserved capacity) — committed discounts, lower $/1M tokens if you can commit to a baseline (we’ll model 120M and 300M commits).

Sean/Dylan — can you run a quick unit-economic model (generation tokens $/1M, embeddings $/1k vectors) for: hosted US, hosted EU (+ expected premium), and 12-month reserved commit levels at 120M and 300M tokens/month? Include an example P&L that maps to James’s $24k–$72k annual band and show the target $/1M tokens for each. Also confirm whether embeddings pricing is regional or flat.

James — assuming you can confirm the pilot split (EU vs US traffic) we’ll fold residency into the cost model. If the EU portion is large, we may recommend a Dedicated capacity in EU to hit the $6–$10/1M target.

I’ve attached the SOC2 evidence request doc they mentioned — they’ll need it for security/compliance review.

Marissa

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, James Park <james@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Pricing & regional residency (FinTechCo)

Thanks for the details, James — good context. Quick summary of the numbers and what we can offer:

1) Baseline list pricing (hosted):
   - Generation: $12.00 per 1M tokens (US hosted endpoints)
   - Embeddings: $0.75 per 1k vectors (US hosted)

2) EU hosted premium: ~+18% on the token/unit price (typical range 15–20%) because of regional infra, throughput constraints on smaller regions, and added compliance operational costs. That maps to about $14.16 / 1M tokens and $0.89 per 1k vectors in EU-hosted list pricing.

3) Committed / Dedicated (12-month reserved capacity) examples (EU or US location selectable):
   - Commit: 120M tokens/month -> effective blended rate ~ $7.50 / 1M tokens (generation)
   - Commit: 300M tokens/month -> effective blended rate ~ $5.50 / 1M tokens
   - Embeddings discounted similarly (roughly 30–40% off list with commit).

Notes on residency and economics: if FinTechCo needs EU-only processing for a large share of traffic, a Dedicated EU pool (12-month commit) typically gives the best path to hit the $6–$10 / 1M token target while meeting residency. Hosted EU endpoints will be higher per token but faster to stand up for a pilot; Dedicated requires procurement lead time but is cost-efficient at scale.

Quick mapping to James’s bands:
   - Pilot (30M/month, hosted EU for EU traffic + hosted US for non-EU): expect monthly cost ~$420 (EU portion upweighted) — fits pilot band.
   - Steady (120M/month): Hosted list EU mix -> ~ $1,700–$2,200/month; Dedicated 120M commit -> ~$900/month equivalent (depending on exact EU/US split).
   - Peak (300M/month): Dedicated 300M commit would get you into the $1,650/month equivalent range (~$5.50/1M) which is inside the $6–$10 target.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa: send the split (EU vs US %) for pilot and steady state; we’ll produce a 12-month TCO comparison table (Hosted US, Hosted EU, Dedicated EU commit, Dedicated US commit).
- James: if you can indicate a preference on procurement timeline (fast pilot vs commit), we’ll prepare a commercial term sheet.

I’ll turn this into a one-page cost model and send by EOD.

Thanks — Sean
